body:
After some digging through the source code i want to share my thoughts:

The Build Process is implemented via C# Scripts (modules/mono/editor/GodotTools/GodotTools/Build/BuildManager.cs & BuildSystem.cs).
~~The Nodes script (modules/mono/editor/GodotTools/GodotTools/Build/MSBuildPanel.cs) then marshalls **each line** produced by the build process through `CallDeferred`.~~
~~A detailed log of a build (included in the example) contains about 70k lines of text, so that is 70k marshalling operations.~~

~~I think the best option here is to just not update the UI at each line of text received (the application hangs anyways cause it is too much to handle).~~
~~Maybe it would even be okay to just launch a CLI with the dotnet build command and leave that open after execution for inspection by the user.~~
~~Otherwise the only solution i can come up with is reimplementing the Build Process in C++ to avoid marshalling.~~

The Nodes script uses a string add operator, but since strings are immutable in .NET, this leads to some heavy overhead. A String Builder could solve that problem.
